standing: ILLUSTRATIVE AND ANCHOR-ONLY. Items here were selected by salience, not drawn by a content-blind frame. They may serve as evidence anchors for architecture-level signature scores, and they may be rendered as illustration. They MAY NOT enter the directional test, because a set assembled by noticing cannot answer the selection-on-the-dependent-variable charge. That is what the frames are for.
provenance: Every item was verified against published reporting in this session. Dates, case names, votes and figures are as reported by the cited sources. No item was supplied from Claude's prior knowledge without a source, and no figure was estimated.

items.title: Trump v. IRS suit, voluntary dismissal, and the $1.776 billion Anti-Weaponization Fund
items.what_is_established: Trump, Donald Jr., Eric and the Trump Organization sued the IRS and Treasury on 2026-01-29 under IRC section 7431 over the Littlejohn disclosure of tax data, claiming at least $10 billion on the theory that each view of a news article containing the leaked data was a separate $1,000 statutory violation. A voluntary dismissal was filed 2026-05-18, two days before a court deadline, the notice stating the dismissal was available as of right. An order by Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche established an Anti-Weaponization Fund and directed Treasury to transfer $1.776 billion from the Judgment Fund to an account for its sole use.
items.matches_book: Part VII, the $1.776B audit-bar structure. The figure and the self-executing dismissal are corroborated.

items.title: DOJ addendum barring IRS audit of Trump and family
items.what_is_established: A DOJ addendum to the settlement barred the IRS from auditing Trump and his family, reported by ABC News and Newsweek in May 2026. On 2026-08-03 the Acting Attorney General's rescission order restricted the audit-immunity provision to apply only retroactively, to claims that existed when the settlement occurred, so that it no longer shelters future tax filings.

contestation.summary: PolitiFact treated the durability of a 'forever' bar as an open question in May; the August order then narrowed it in writing. The surviving capture is the retroactive bar on pre-settlement matters, which is narrower than the book's Part VII describes.

items.matches_book: PARTIAL. Part VII describes the family as 'forever barred' for any matter predating the agreement. As of 2026-08-03 the bar is retroactive-only in writing. The structure the book scores, a self-executing dismissal used to obtain an audit bar, still holds; its scope is now narrower and the /sabbot anchor text needs the August narrowing added.

items.title: January 6 participants not excluded from fund eligibility
items.what_is_established: Acting Attorney General Blanche declined to rule out January 6 rioters receiving payouts from the fund. Senate Republicans objected. Senate Judiciary Democrats pressed Blanche on the point.
items.explicit_non_claim: This is a refusal to exclude, NOT a decision to pay January 6 participants. No payment to a January 6 participant from this fund is established, and the fund was later rescinded. Coding this as a directed payment would be exactly the projection-stated-as-event failure Part III forbids.

items.title: Judicial halt and compelled disclosure, then rescission of the fund
items.what_is_established: U.S. District Judge Leonie Brinkema, Eastern District of Virginia, halted work on the fund on 2026-05-29 and ordered Trump officials to disclose who set it up. Plaintiffs were Democracy Forward and Common Cause, filing for a former January 6 prosecutor terminated by DOJ and a professor previously acquitted of assaulting federal agents; grounds included a collusive agreement circumventing the Appropriations Clause, with separate suits raising the Domestic Emoluments Clause. Two Capitol Police officers also sued on 2026-05-20. DOJ argued in June filings that the fund was not proceeding. On the evening of 2026-08-03 Acting Attorney General Blanche issued an order stating that the 2026-05-18 order establishing the fund 'is rescinded and shall have no force or effect', and that no members were appointed, no funds were transferred, no claims process was established and no claims were paid. The order followed negotiations with Senators Tillis and Cornyn, who conditioned his confirmation on eliminating the fund in writing.
items.explicit_non_claim: This is civil litigation with compelled discovery, NOT a criminal or judicial investigation into illegality. The distinction matters: a court ordering disclosure in a civil case is a different object from an investigation, and overstating it is the kind of error a hostile reader uses to void a row.
items.sequence_note: Order of events: fund ordered 05-18; suits 05-20 to 05-22; judicial halt and disclosure order 05-29; DOJ 'not proceeding' filings in June; written rescission 08-03. An earlier draft of this annex implied the rescission preceded the halt; it did not.

items.title: Trump v. Boyle: removal of Consumer Product Safety Commission members permitted
items.what_is_established: On 2025-07-23 the Supreme Court granted a stay in Trump v. Boyle, docket 25A11, 6-3, of the District of Maryland's 2025-06-13 order, permitting removal of CPSC members Mary Boyle, Alexander Hoehn-Saric and Richard Trumka Jr. Kagan dissented, joined by Sotomayor and Jackson; Kavanaugh concurred. Emergency docket, not a merits decision.
items.correction: This is the CONSUMER PRODUCT SAFETY Commission, not food safety. Federal food-safety capacity was reduced through FDA and USDA staffing actions, which are administrative and belong in a separate row with their own anchors. Conflating the two puts a checkable error into the register.

items.title: Trump v. Slaughter: Humphrey's Executor overruled
items.what_is_established: On 2026-06-29 the Supreme Court held 6-3 that for-cause removal protections for heads of agencies exercising executive power violate separation of powers, overruling Humphrey's Executor. Affected bodies include the FTC, Consumer Product Safety Commission, Nuclear Regulatory Commission, FERC, Federal Labor Relations Authority, FEC and Surface Transportation Board. Carve-outs: bodies exercising no part of the executive power such as GAO, investigative-only oversight boards, non-Article III courts, and the Federal Reserve Board of Governors as a special arrangement sanctioned by history. The dissent records that the government conceded the majority's logic extends to inferior officers and perhaps to career civil servants, and the majority did not disavow that concession. Arnold & Porter's July 2026 advisory states the decision reaches heads of multi-member independent agencies exercising rulemaking, adjudication and civil enforcement power, naming the FTC, SEC and CFTC, with the Federal Reserve carved out on grounds of unique historical status rather than function.
items.scope_note: The holding covers multi-member independent agencies. It does not by its terms reach food-safety or food-and-agriculture bodies, whose senior officials are presidential appointees already removable at will, nor does it expressly reach Inspectors General or administrative law judges. The load-bearing expansion for the register is the uncontested concession about inferior officers and career civil servants, which is on the record from the government's own submission and is a firmer anchor than any inferred extension.

items.title: Learning Resources v. Trump: IEEPA tariffs held unauthorized
items.what_is_established: On 2026-02-20 the Supreme Court held 6-3 in Learning Resources, Inc. v. Trump, docket 24-1287, that IEEPA does not authorize the President to impose tariffs; authority to regulate importation does not reach tariff-setting, a core Article I taxing function. Roberts wrote the majority, joined in relevant parts by Sotomayor, Kagan, Gorsuch, Barrett and Jackson. Thomas and Kavanaugh dissented, Alito joining Kavanaugh. The opinion did not address refunds of tariffs already collected.
items.why_this_item_matters_most: This is a Supreme Court decision AGAINST the administration's largest economic action, from the same Court that expanded removal power. It is the single most useful item in this annex, because it is a discriminating datum: it shows the judicial locus is not uniformly directional. An instrument that cannot represent this cannot claim to be measuring rather than asserting.

items.title: Canada tariffs re-imposed under Section 338 after the IEEPA ruling
items.what_is_established: Following the IEEPA ruling, three presidential proclamations signed 2026-07-20 imposed 50 percent tariffs on a broad range of Canadian products, effective 2026-08-22 after a delay from 2026-08-19, invoking Section 338 of the Tariff Act of 1930. Canada announced counter-tariffs in August 2026, effective 2026-09-08: tiered at 15, 25 and 50 percent across approximately C$27.6 billion of U.S. imports spanning 629 HS codes, including steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp, paper and electronics, with certain existing 25 percent tariffs raised to 50 percent to match the U.S. rates. Trump set out further moves after the Canadian measures took effect, and separately stated he was raising the new global tariff rate to 15 percent after the Supreme Court loss.

contestation.summary: Whether Section 338 supplies lawful authority for these tariffs is unresolved and in litigation commentary.

items.note_for_T2: The re-imposition under a second statute after the first was struck is a candidate S3 anti-remediation anchor: the cheapest available fix was to accept the ruling. It cuts against the predicted low S1, so T2's prediction should be locked with this item already in view.
items.amended: 2026-09-12: dates corrected. The first draft recorded the action as July 2026 from a White House fact sheet date; the proclamations were signed 2026-07-20 and the tariffs took effect 2026-08-22. The escalation is an August and September event, not a July one.

items.title: Strikes on Iran without congressional authorization
items.what_is_established: Joint U.S.-Israel airstrikes on 2026-02-28 resulted in the death of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Further U.S. strikes were reported 2026-06-28. Trump asserted Commander in Chief authority; Rubio stated congressional leadership was notified and that no law required it. Congress did not authorize the strikes; H.J.Res.176, a 2026 AUMF against Iran, was introduced. Oona Hathaway called the strikes blatantly illegal under U.S. and international law; Peter Shane noted the constitutional question is disputed.
items.explicit_non_claim: That strikes occurred without authorization is established. Calling it a war is a contested legal characterization, not a documented fact, and should be tagged contested if it appears in a row.

items.title: Maritime strike campaign on alleged drug vessels
items.what_is_established: 68 strikes and 227 deaths including 23 missing and presumed dead, with 3 known survivors, as of 2026-08-26. Two War Powers resolutions failed in December 2025; a Senate joint resolution on Venezuela advanced 52-47 on 2026-01-08 and failed 50-50 on 2026-01-14 with the Vice President breaking the tie. The UN Security Council held an emergency meeting 2025-12-23; four UN experts condemned the naval blockade on 2025-12-24 as illegal armed aggression. Families of men killed have brought wrongful-death claims; the ACLU filed on behalf of families of Trinidadian men killed in a strike; a family of dead fishermen has alleged murder.

contestation.summary: Whether specific victims were fishermen rather than traffickers is disputed per strike and is the subject of active litigation. The aggregate death figure is not disputed; the characterization of individual victims is.

items.could_not_verify: The claim that the munitions used cost roughly one million dollars each was not established by any source located. Munition type and unit cost should be dropped from any row unless a procurement or DoD source is produced. An unsourced cost figure in a row about deaths is the fastest way to lose the row.

items.title: Mail-voting executive order and its litigation
items.what_is_established: Nineteen states sued over the elections executive order on 2025-04-03, arguing it is unconstitutional. A federal court blocked the U.S. Postal Service from implementing the order's mail-voting restrictions. On 2026-08-24 the Supreme Court lifted one of two injunctions, allowing the order to move forward in part pending challenges; the administration subsequently asked the Court to clear the way for full implementation.

items.title: The $2,000 tariff dividend promised and not delivered
items.what_is_established: Trump promised $2,000 tariff dividend checks by mid-2026, announced 2025-11-17. ABC News reported ten months later that they had not materialized. CNBC reported on 2026-02-23 that experts put the odds at effectively zero.
items.why_stronger_than_the_5k_item: Non-delivery against a dated public commitment is a documented event. A promise not yet due is not.

items.title: The $5,000 payment promise conditioned on a Republican congressional win
items.what_is_established: On 2026-09-10 Trump promised $5,000 payments conditioned on Republicans keeping control of Congress. The proposal drew bipartisan criticism, including Republican figures calling it vote-buying. Legal scholars publicly analysed how federal anti-bribery law applies. NBC News and CNBC reported the plan as impractical and over $1 trillion in cost.
items.explicit_non_claim: That the promise was made is established. That it is illegal is an argued legal question raised by commentators, not an adjudicated fact, and must be tagged contested. No enforcement action is established.

items.title: Hospital closures and coverage loss
items.what_is_established: Becker's reported four hospital closures in 2026. Urban Institute and Robert Wood Johnson Foundation published analysis of hospital financial and workforce strain under OBBBA in July 2026. Michigan reporting describes rural hospitals closing or reducing service after Medicaid cuts.
items.projected_component: Figures in the hundreds are AT RISK counts, not closures: a Forbes analysis puts 446 hospitals at risk; a separate analysis put 55 additional rural hospitals at risk. CBO-class coverage figures, including 2.2 million losing insurance in 2026 if enhanced ACA subsidies expire, are projections on stated horizons.
items.tagging_rule: The four closures are occurred. Everything in the hundreds or millions is projected and must carry that tag every time it appears. This is the row where a single slip voids the section, because it is the row a hostile reviewer checks first.

items.title: Federal food-safety capacity reduced by administrative action
items.what_is_established: The National Advisory Committee on Microbiological Criteria for Foods, established 1988, and the National Advisory Committee on Meat and Poultry Inspection, established 1971, were terminated as of 2025-03-07, with no statement issued by the administration or any federal public health agency at the time. NACMCF had been reviewing regulatory approaches to Listeria monocytogenes after the Boar's Head outbreak and Cronobacter in infant formula. USDA reduced its workforce by 18 percent between January and June; the Food Safety and Inspection Service lost about 9 percent of its staff and did not recover the 775 employees it lost. Consumer complaints on meat, poultry and egg products rose nearly 40 percent, from 1,443 to 2,016. FDA fired and then moved to rehire some human-foods staff.
items.correlation_not_causation: The complaint increase alongside the staffing reduction is a measured co-occurrence. The reporting does not establish a causal relationship and neither does this record. Any row using both figures carries the correlation tag, and causal language is available only with temporal precedence, a documented mechanism, and confounds eliminated.
items.why_this_is_the_right_row: This is what the food-safety claim actually rests on, and it is a separate decision locus from the judicial one. It is also a cleaner S2 anchor than any removal ruling: an advisory committee terminated with no public statement, while the enforcement and inspection apparatus continues operating, is precisely the selectivity S2 reads. Attaching it to the judicial locus would both misstate the holding and lose an independent locus, which is the one quantity the register cannot spare.

items.title: Pentagon press-credential pledge; press corps turns in badges
items.what_is_established: On 2025-10-15 nearly every major outlet — Axios, Fox News, NBC, ABC, CNN, NPR, AP, the Washington Post, the New York Times — turned in Pentagon access badges rather than sign a new reporting pledge they said would criminalize national-security reporting and expose signatories to prosecution; the Pentagon confiscated the badges. One America News indicated it would sign. Roughly fifteen reporters remained. Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell: the policy is 'what's best for our troops and the national security of this country.' The Pentagon Press Association called it 'a dark day for press freedom.'
items.explicit_non_claim: 'Willingly' is only technically accurate: the choice offered was sign or leave. Coding this as a voluntary departure would misstate the mechanism.
items.base_rate_role: Control case for the forecast PRED-2026-09-22: at eleven months the policy stands and access has not been restored.

items.title: Associated Press v. Budowich: injunction, non-compliance, appellate narrowing, no decision at nineteen months
items.what_is_established: Judge McFadden granted a preliminary injunction on 2025-04-08 holding the government 'cannot exclude journalists purely based on their viewpoints' (780 F.Supp.3d 32). AP moved to enforce on 2025-04-16 alleging non-compliance, including being barred from an Oval Office event despite the order; enforcement was denied. On 2025-06-06 the D.C. Circuit stayed the injunction except as to the East Room, Judge Rao reasoning that the Oval Office and Air Force One are 'not public' and the president may discriminate by viewpoint there. En banc rehearing denied 2025-07-22. Argued 2025-11-24. No decision as of 2026-09-22.
items.counter_directional_component: The East Room injunction survived appeal. Within this locus that is a partial counter item and is recorded as such.
items.base_rate_role: Pilot for the forecast: the cheap fix was ordered, disobeyed, narrowed, and left undecided. Nineteen months from filing.

items.title: White House bans CNN, MS NOW and Politico; credentials disabled without notice
items.what_is_established: On Friday 2026-09-18 the President announced by Truth Social that he was banning 'Fake News CNN, MSNOW... and Politico... from the White House as a result of their constant "reporting" fake news.' Reporters found their badges disabled at the entrance over the weekend, without notice or process. The White House Correspondents' Association reported the President describing the action in the Oval Office as 'a ban on the free press.' The three outlets sued on Monday 2026-09-21: 'Without notice or process, the White House revoked our journalists' credentials because it objected to our reporting.' Theodore Boutrous: the ban 'is, on its face, unconstitutional.'
items.intent_on_the_record: Per the book's two-registers rule: the actor's own characterization — 'a ban on the free press' — is quoted, not inferred. It is reported by the WHCA as the President's words in the Oval Office; the public framing the same day was 'fake news'. That pairing is the S5 internal/external mismatch stated by the actor.

contestation.summary: Administration defenders compare the ban to the 2023 hard-pass rule change, under which the count fell from 1,417 to 975 (442 fewer) over three months. The 2023 change was a reapplication under published eligibility criteria (full-time employment, D.C. residence, regular coverage, gallery accreditation, Secret Service check) applied to every holder; the 2026 action names three outlets by their coverage. The number is recorded so the comparison is argued on its mechanism, not dismissed. Fact-checks distinguishing the two are on record; the register does not adopt their rating.

items.title: Five-network TV pool suspends coverage of presidential events
items.what_is_established: On Monday 2026-09-21 Fox News pool chair Bryan Boughton notified pool subscribers that the TV pool would halt coverage of 'events designated as pool coverage of the President,' with 'no replacement pool put in place. All other pool coverage will continue as normal, including Congress, VIPs, and selected events.' ABC, CBS, NBC, Fox and CNN issued a joint statement: 'No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.' Real America's Voice was reported as the only station in the out-of-town traveling pool.

contestation.summary: Whether the suspension is a 'win' is a contested reading. For: unprecedented cross-network solidarity including Fox; courts backed the press in 2018 (Acosta) and 2025 (AP, East Room). Against: the boycott delivers, at the press corps's own cost, the outcome the ban sought — no independent video of the president — and the Pentagon control case shows a walkout unremedied at eleven months. Salon's time-shape point: legal victory is probable and months out, past the midterm window.

items.explicit_non_claim: This is a press-side action responding to the ban, not an administration decision; it does not constitute its own decision locus. Print and wire pool participation is not established in the sources located.

items.title: Paramount Skydance–Warner Bros. Discovery: state settlement clears a Trump-cleared sale of CNN to the Ellisons within days of the ban
items.what_is_established: Twelve state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America settled their suit against the $110 billion Paramount Skydance (Larry Ellison) acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery on 2026-09-21. Terms reported: independent editorial boards for CNN and CBS; headcount requirements for journalists at both; a $30 million penalty tied to film output; worker protections. The administration had already cleared the deal. Closing by 2026-09-30 avoids a $7 million per day penalty to Warner shareholders. David Ellison: CNN will operate independently, 'we want to be in the truth business.' Seth Stern, Freedom of the Press Foundation: 'An independent editorial board for CNN and CBS is a weak half-measure.' The Ellisons already control Paramount and CBS News.

contestation.summary: Whether the editorial boards protect independence is disputed; their duration and enforcement mechanism are not specified in the sources located. This is the condition P3 measures at T+365.

items.structural_note: The entity that revoked CNN's credentials on 2026-09-18/19 is the entity that cleared CNN's sale. That is the S3 → S1 chain shape in Part VII, recorded here as documented sequence, not as an inference about motive.

items.title: A White-House-selected second TV slot sat in every daily pool before the ban
items.what_is_established: The White House's own weekly press-rotation announcements, republished in the pool-report archive, list two TV slots per day: a primary slot rotating among ABC, CBS, CNN, FOX and NBC, and a 'Secondary TV' slot filled by the White House from a different set. For 4–17 September the secondary assignments were RAV, RSBN, OAN, Univision, Lindell TV, Scripps, Newsmax, FOX 5 DC, Sinclair, Bloomberg TV, NewsNation, CBN, GB News and Univision. A 'New Media' slot is likewise filled daily (NOTUS, Spot On, Zero Hedge, The Federalist, Gateway Pundit, Heartlander News, Frontlines, Human Events, UnHerd, Townhall, National Review, NTD, Center Square, Semafor). When the five networks suspended pool coverage on 21 September, the secondary slot became the only TV in the pool.

contestation.summary: Which secondary-slot outlets are 'administration-aligned' is a characterization, not a fact in the rotation. The list is recorded so the classification is argued, not assumed. Two are anchored elsewhere: OAN signed the Pentagon pledge (AX-016); RAV was alone in the traveling pool after 21 Sept (AX-019).

items.why_it_matters: P3 predicts substitution rather than vacuum. This item shows the substitute was seated in advance: the structure that fills the gap did not have to be built after the ban.

items.title: Department of War endorses the White House ban the day it is announced
items.what_is_established: On 2026-09-18 the Secretary of War posted from @SecWar on X that the Department 'fully supports President Trump's decision to kick CNN, MSNBCNOW and Politico to the curb', that the outlets had 'self-deported' from the Pentagon rather than accept its credential rules (AX-016), and that they had 'endangered our troops with false stories, leaks, and trafficked in fiction and lies about the President, our Warriors, and their mission.' No example of a false story or a leak was given in the statement.

contestation.summary: The endangerment and leak claims are the actor's assertions and are unsubstantiated in the statement itself; they are recorded as statements, not as established facts about the outlets.

items.why_it_matters: The locus rule counts decisions, not headlines. The Pentagon pledge (2025-10) and the White House ban (2026-09) were entered as one locus on the ground that credential access is decided at one place. A same-day endorsement of the second by the author of the first, citing the first, is the corroboration that reading needed. It does not raise the count; it confirms that the count should not be raised.

items.title: The suit: Judge Kelly assigned, hearing set for 23 Sept, appeal vowed before any ruling
items.what_is_established: On Saturday 2026-09-19 Secret Service and White House security officers deactivated and in some cases confiscated the hard passes of Akayla Gardner (MS NOW), Betsy Klein (CNN) and Cheyenne Haslett (Politico) at the gate. On Monday 2026-09-21 CNN, MS NOW and Politico, represented by Gibson Dunn, filed in the U.S. District Court for D.C. seeking a temporary restraining order restoring access; the case was assigned to Judge Timothy J. Kelly, a 2017 Trump appointee who in November 2018 ordered Jim Acosta's credential restored on due-process grounds. The government's response was due 2026-09-22; the TRO hearing was set for Wednesday 2026-09-23 at 3:30 p.m. by videoconference. At 3:39 p.m. on 21 Sept the President posted that the plaintiffs 'have drawn a great Judge, for them, a man who ruled in favor of Jim Acosta ... sadly, appointed by "TRUMP"', and that 'almost without question and, as usual, we'll go for appeal', asking 'Why should I have to give "access" to such people?'

contestation.summary: Whether an appeal follows a ruling is a future event; the vow is recorded as a statement made before any ruling existed. The docket number reported by one secondary source could not be confirmed and is omitted.

items.why_it_matters: P1 says the credentials will not be restored by voluntary act before a court compels it. An appeal announced two days before the first hearing is the cheap fix declined in advance, in the actor's words. It is the first dated observation on P1, and it is consistent with the base-rate case (AP v. Budowich: ordered, disobeyed, narrowed). The 23 Sept hearing is P1's first checkpoint.

items.title: Intent restated in the actor's words: 'not an assault on the Free Press ... an assault on the FAKE NEWS'
items.what_is_established: At 7:53 a.m. on 2026-09-21 the President posted: 'The White House is not instituting an assault on the Free Press, something which I cherish. It is instituting an assault on the FAKE NEWS ... It is a threat to our National Security, and must be stopped, NOW!' Three days earlier the WHCA had reported his description of the same action in the Oval Office as 'a ban on the free press' (AX-018).

contestation.summary: The Oval Office phrase is reported by the WHCA, not recorded on tape in any source located; the Truth Social text is verbatim from the platform mirror. The two registers are therefore not of equal provenance, and the item says so.

items.why_it_matters: S5 reads the distance between internal and external accounts of the same act. Here the external account is supplied by the actor in writing, the internal one by the press corps' report of his spoken words. The written register also supplies the 'National Security' ground that the appeal vow (AX-023) repeats, which is the ground a court would be asked to defer to.

items.title: Day one without the pool: an inaudible event, then 'Trump TV: The Essentials Station'
items.what_is_established: On the first day of the five-network suspension (AX-019), the President's helipad ribbon-cutting at the White House produced footage with no usable audio: clips circulated from attendees' phones, and a Newsmax anchor said on air that there was no microphone because the pool cameras were not there. At 7 p.m. the same day the White House launched a round-the-clock livestream, 'Trump TV: The Essentials Station', described by deputy assistant Kaelan Dorr as 'a livestream of the Administration's greatest hits, unfiltered', alongside promotion of the White House app for events 'streamed DIRECTLY to your phone'.

contestation.summary: That the channel's comment feature is turned off is stated by one source (Richardson, 21 Sept) and was not independently confirmed; it is recorded as single-source. The audio failure is one event; its cause (pool absence versus Marine One noise) is asserted by observers, not established.

items.why_it_matters: P3 predicts substitution rather than vacuum. This is the vacuum and the substitute on the same calendar day: an event without independent sound, and an administration-produced feed announced within hours. It is one day and is not a share; the B-series counts (BASELINE-2026-09-22) are what P3 is scored against at T+365. The pre-seated secondary TV slot (AX-021) and this feed are the two substitution channels the re-count must keep separate.

items.title: The substitution channels predate the ban; the vacancy is what is new
items.what_is_established: White House Wire, a link-aggregation site, launched 2025-05-01 ('a place for supporters of the president's agenda to get the real news', a White House official to Axios). A 'Media Bias' portal followed in December 2025. The White House app launched 2026-03-27 with livestreams, alerts and 'unfiltered, real-time updates straight from the source'; in May 2026 the federal chief information officer directed agency CIOs to auto-install it on government-issued iPhones and iPads, which the FAA's notice described as 'mandated by the White House'. A White-House-selected secondary TV slot sat in every daily pool through the baseline window (AX-021). 'Trump TV: The Essentials Station' launched 2026-09-21 at 19:00 EDT, seven hours after the five-network suspension (AX-025). Of these, only Trump TV postdates the ban.
items.inclusion_rule: A substitution channel is one that originates or carries presidential-event footage a pool camera would otherwise have produced. Counted: the secondary TV slot (originates; the only substitute with a camera in the room), Trump TV (originates), the White House app (carries; the one compelled distribution channel). Excluded by the rule and recorded as adjacent structure: White House Wire (aggregates links, originates nothing) and the Media Bias portal (complaints intake, no footage). The rule was fixed before the count and is not chosen by reference to what was vacated. What was vacated is one rotating pool-camera slot and three outlets' credentials, one of them print; the two sides share no unit except footage share by origin, which is the unit P3 is scored in.

contestation.summary: Whether the app 'carries' pool-equivalent footage or merely relays administration-produced video is the line between carrier and originator; both are administration-origin for P3 purposes, so the distinction does not move the share. The Axios quotation is as reported by Wikipedia's summary of Axios and was not read at source.

items.why_it_matters: S3 reads the sequence, and the sequence here is build, distribute, seat, then remove. The channels that fill the gap were launched between four and seventeen months before the gap existed and one of them was placed on federal devices by mandate. The order rules out one direction — the channels were not built to fill a vacancy that did not yet exist — and does not establish the other; nothing here shows the channels' existence caused the removal, and the item does not claim it. What the order removes is the reading of the vacancy as an unplanned loss the administration then improvised around. (An earlier wording said the removal 'cannot be scored as a reaction to the networks' withdrawal'; that was chronology, not a finding — the credentials were pulled on 18–19 September and the networks withdrew on the 21st — and it is corrected here rather than deleted.) Same shape as the fund and the audit bar: the beneficiary structure exists before the act that routes to it. For P3, 'administration feed' now has a launch history rather than a single day, and the T+365 re-count applies the inclusion rule above without revisiting it.

locus_summary.LOCUS-DOJ-AWF: One locus. Four annex items, one decision chain.
locus_summary.LOCUS-SCOTUS-REMOVAL: One locus. Boyle and Slaughter are the same Court on the same question.
locus_summary.LOCUS-SCOTUS-TARIFF: One locus, opposite direction from the removal locus.
locus_summary.LOCUS-MARITIME-STRIKES: One locus for the campaign; individual strikes are not independent decisions.
locus_summary.reading: Twenty-six verified items collapse to twelve independent loci, one running counter-directional and one carrying a partial counter item. A sign test on that is worthless, which is why this annex is anchor-only and the frames carry the statistic. The press-access chain added one locus despite ten items, because the codebook collapses arguable boundaries to the coarser unit.
locus_summary.LOCUS-FOOD-SAFETY: One locus. Administrative, not judicial. Independent of the removal line.
locus_summary.LOCUS-PRESS-ACCESS: One locus, collapsed per the coarser-is-conservative rule: Pentagon (Department of Defense, 2025-10), AP (Executive Office, 2025-02 →) and the CNN / MS NOW / Politico ban (Executive Office, 2026-09) are one executive press-access policy with three dated instances. Splitting Defense from the Executive Office is arguable and would add a locus; not taken, and AX-022 (the Department's same-day endorsement citing its own pledge) is the corroboration the collapse rested on. The East Room injunction is a partial counter item inside the locus.
locus_summary.LOCUS-MEDIA-CONSOLIDATION: One locus. Private transaction, state settlement, federal clearance; independent of the press-access decision chain though coupled to it in P3.
